items.finding: geodawn_dem_a2_100m.tif (used only to infer dip polarity) has an x-origin of 243349.9656 m instead of 243350 m (0.034 m offset).

Cutting visible polylines at the withheld + 3 px collar mask creates artificial 'cut tips' next to withheld truth (254 in draw seed 20). Using them would leak the withheld location into the corridor generator.
items.handling: Cut tips are excluded from corridor generation in every holdout run (conservative; the live catalogue has no cut tips). Counted in evidence/e2_gate.json tip receipts.

items.finding: The catalogue hide-and-recover instrument measures how withheld catalogue components cluster around visible ones. A sibling measured its rank correlation with 12 owner-reported live scores at +0.14, and here a distance-only halo is the strongest arm. Passing it is necessary, not sufficient, for a live gain.
items.handling: Gate decided on the instrument as pre-registered; the limitation is stated in the run card and README.

items.finding: The live hidden-truth size |G| = 12,226 px used to set the live greedy bar is a model (GEMSDOE32 inversion of owner-reported scores), not an organizer number.
items.handling: Labelled [model]; it changes only how many dots the live build places, not the holdout verdict.

items.finding: The hard-linked-ramp masking test is weakly discriminating: masking a link turns its two attachment points into the very tips the generator pairs, so a random-azimuth line from the same tips already recovers ~70% of link pixels within 300 m.
items.handling: Reported with its null; not used as a gate.

items.finding: 41% of in-footprint INGENIOUS records carry a usable DIPDIRECT; the rest have 'Unspecified' or blank.
items.handling: Dip polarity inferred from hanging-wall topography (lower side) where unrecorded; agreement with recorded dips 90.3% on 1,984 polylines (evidence/e1_first_test.json).

items.finding: The protocol's 70% / 3-px dot-overlap rule cannot discriminate against space-filling registry rasters. Example: r14_union_tips10_lat6.tif is a uniform 6-px lattice (3.7% support, so the template classifies it as a dot field) whose 3-px halo covers 76% of all allowed cells; random dots placed in this lane's corridor band score 0.785 against it, exactly the geometric expectation pi/4. Any candidate in that domain 'fails' the rule regardless of method.
items.handling: Logged conservatively as duplicate-by-rule with a per-firing diagnostic (halo coverage, random-dot baseline, excess over random) in evidence/e3_uniqueness.json. Template gap reported in the run card with a proposed fix (classify by halo coverage and test firings against random dots in the candidate's own domain); vendor/gems57 not edited (no private fork).

items.finding: Tooling: in a blob-less partial clone, `git ls-tree -l` lazily downloads every blob to report sizes, which stalled the first registry scan on large repositories.
items.handling: scripts/fetch_registry.py lists HEAD trees with one REST git/trees call per repository instead; full scan of 862 rasters, 0 errors.
